title: Day One Is Brave
body: Your uterus is doing real, hormone-driven work right now. Estrogen and progesterone have both dropped, which is exactly why energy feels low — your body is literally renewing itself. That dip is not weakness, it's biology.
tip: Cancel the optional plans. A warm drink, soft clothes, and zero guilt about resting today.

title: Why Cramps Happen
body: Cramps come from prostaglandins — chemicals your uterus releases to help shed its lining. More prostaglandins = stronger cramps. The good news: anti-inflammatory foods, heat, and gentle movement can genuinely help.
tip: Heat pad on the lower belly for 15 minutes. Magnesium-rich foods (dark chocolate, almonds) help too.

title: Iron Matters Today
body: Period blood contains iron, and replenishing it matters more than people realize. Low iron can amplify fatigue and brain fog. Pairing iron-rich foods with vitamin C boosts absorption.
tip: Spinach + lemon juice. Lentils + tomato. Steak + orange. Tiny pairings, real difference.

companionVariants.owl: Sage notes: vitamin C converts non-heme iron to absorbable form 🦉
companionVariants.blossom: Feed yourself well today 🩷 You deserve real food

title: Energy Is Returning
body: Estrogen is just starting to rise again. You might notice your mood lifting and the heaviness lifting too. It's the first signal of the follicular phase — your body's spring is approaching.
tip: A short walk outside today. Sunlight + movement = mood medicine.

title: Hydration Hero
body: You lose more fluid than you realize during your period — between blood, sweat, and the bloating shift. Dehydration sneaks in as headaches, fatigue, and worse cramps.
tip: Aim for one extra glass of water today. Add lemon or cucumber if plain feels boring.

title: Period Is Wrapping
body: The flow tapers, hormones start their climb, and your body shifts gears. Many people feel a subtle 'reset' around this point — like a fresh start. It's real, and it's your biology at work.
tip: Set one small intention for this new cycle. Just one. Make it gentle.

title: Bridge Days
body: If you're still here in your menstrual phase past day 7, that's worth tracking. Longer periods can be totally normal for you — but consistent patterns (and changes from your norm) are useful info for any future doctor visit.
tip: Note today's flow and any symptoms in your log. Future-you will thank you.

title: Stretch It Out
body: Gentle yoga and stretching genuinely help with lingering pelvic tension. Cat-cow and child's pose specifically target the lower back and hips where menstrual ache loves to settle.
tip: Five minutes of cat-cow before bed. That's it. That's the whole tip.

title: Pain Check
body: Some discomfort is normal. Pain so bad it stops you from going about your day is not — that's a signal worth investigating. Endometriosis affects 1 in 10 people, and it's often missed for years.
tip: If pain regularly disrupts your life, save your symptom log to share with a doctor.

title: Long Cycle, Real Talk
body: Cycles longer than 35 days can happen naturally, but they can also point to PCOS, thyroid imbalance, stress, or other shifts. None of this is alarming on its own — it's just information.
tip: Track length over 3 cycles to spot a real pattern. One outlier doesn't mean much.

title: Be Your Own Advocate
body: When you go to a doctor, vague descriptions ('it's bad') don't land as well as specific ones ('day 22 to 26, intensity 7/10, every cycle for 6 months'). Tracking turns vague into actionable.
tip: Your symptom log is doctor-ready. Use it.

title: Patience With Patterns
body: Sometimes hormones take time to settle, especially after stress, illness, travel, or going on/off birth control. A few odd cycles in a row aren't a verdict — they're a phase.
tip: Give your body 2-3 cycles to find its rhythm. Track gently, judge nothing.
